title: Angular
blurb: Components, DI, RxJS, routing, forms and change detection.

quiz.question: What are Angular signals?
options: Reactive values that track their readers so Angular updates only what depends on them
quiz.explanation: signal(), computed() and effect() give fine-grained reactivity; templates that read a signal re-render when it changes, enabling zoneless change detection.

quiz.question: What does ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush do?
options: Checks the component only when inputs change by reference, an event fires inside it, an async pipe or signal it reads emits, or it's marked dirty
Runs change detection on every timer tick
quiz.explanation: OnPush skips subtrees whose inputs haven't changed by reference, which pairs well with immutable data and signals.

quiz.question: Which RxJS operator cancels the previous inner request when a new search term arrives?
quiz.explanation: switchMap unsubscribes from the previous inner observable — ideal for typeahead search. concatMap queues, mergeMap runs in parallel, exhaustMap ignores new values while busy.

quiz.question: Standalone components mean…
options: Components that declare their own imports and don't need an NgModule
Components rendered on the server only
quiz.explanation: Standalone components (the default since Angular 19) import their dependencies directly, so NgModules are optional.

quiz.question: Why should you avoid calling methods in templates like {{ total() }} when total is a plain method?
options: It runs on every change-detection cycle and can be slow
quiz.explanation: Template expressions are re-evaluated on every check. Use a computed() signal, a pure pipe, or a precomputed field. (Calling a signal like count() is fine — it's a cheap read.)

problems.title: Typeahead search
problems.prompt: Build a search box that calls the API at most once per 300 ms pause, skips duplicate terms, and ignores stale responses.
problems.solution: this.results$ = this.term.valueChanges.pipe(debounceTime(300), map(t => t.trim()), distinctUntilChanged(), switchMap(t => t ? this.api.search(t).pipe(catchError(() => of([]))) : of([]))); render with the async pipe (or toSignal) so the subscription is cleaned up automatically.

problems.title: Memory leak hunt
problems.prompt: A component subscribes to a route-params observable in ngOnInit and never unsubscribes. What's the risk and the modern fix?
problems.solution: Long-lived observables keep the callback (and the component) alive after it's destroyed, causing leaks and duplicate work. Use the async pipe or toSignal, or pipe(takeUntilDestroyed()) (from @angular/core/rxjs-interop), which unsubscribes when the component is destroyed.
